source.title: Towards A Unified Conformer Structure: from ASR to ASV Task
source.authors: Dexin Liao; Tao Jiang; Feng Wang; Lin Li; Q. Hong

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAM, motivated by loss-landscape sharpness and generalization, and reports ASV benchmark performance. It does not test the listed versions’ claims about memorization, architecture, optimizers, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports EER and minDCF for ASV models under SAM, regularization, model configuration, and ASR-transfer conditions. These results concern benchmark performance, not the listed versions’ specified measures. Results cited from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The study applies SAM using sharpness-based generalization arguments and reports speaker-verification performance. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with train–test gaps, or any other listed version's effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that LSA and SAM improve ASV Conformer generalization, with SAM especially effective for severely overfitted models, and that ASR transfer yields about 11% relative EER improvement on VoxCeleb and CN-Celeb. They acknowledge that the underlying ASR–ASV relationship remains unclear. These conclusions concern their ASV methods rather than direct tests of the listed versions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Conformer ASV models trained with AdamW and SAM on speech-recognition data; does not use the original methods and measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported ASV test EER varies with SAM and weight decay; the authors also report varying outcomes with model configuration and ASR-transfer setup.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM lowers VoxCeleb-O EER from 1.026 to 0.983 for the smaller Conformer, from 1.771 to 1.459 for the larger model at weight decay 0.05, and from 1.521 to 1.218 for the ASR-transferred larger model at weight decay 0.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM can improve held-out speaker-verification performance in these Conformer configurations; this does not establish the magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the extracted comparisons. Its benchmark EER is not a direct measurement of the train-test gap or the outcomes specified by the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 configuration comparisons and Table 3 ASR-transfer results report ASV benchmark metrics but do not test a listed version; not extracted because the catalog’s version-specific measures are absent. Table 2’s other rows do not add an independently described SAM comparison relevant to the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural versus random labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold; configuration comparisons do not establish this threshold or convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects across data-size, augmentation, and regularization conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No listed version receives a verdict. The study uses unscaled L2-neighborhood SAM and reports test EER, without measuring sharpness or train–test-gap correlations. The width, architecture, and transfer comparisons do not supply the missing version-specific tests.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the stated connectivity comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparison under the stated tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects under the specified data-size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its association with the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
